value: males answered a visual-only stimulus (artificial foot flag) with foot flags, but fewer than to acoustic stimuli (GLMM pair-wise P = 0.007)
method: field playback to calling males at a stream: a painted model frog with an extendable artificial leg and a loudspeaker about 50 cm from the focal male, three stimulus types (acoustic: three calls; visual: three foot flags; multimodal: call plus flag), each 30 s followed by a 90 s control period after a 60 s baseline; responses scored as calls, taps and foot flags; GLMM
conditions: 31 S. parvus males tested in Ulu Temburong National Park, Brunei, March to April 2010 (Methods); individuals recognised by dorsal pattern to avoid retesting; stimulus order counterbalanced; the artificial foot was white (about 100% reflectance) or dark grey (about 10%) and the Discussion calls the lack of a difference between the white and grey foot unexpected; the paper does not say whether playback males were wild-caught or how many males did not respond, and only recordings in which the focal male could be observed through the whole presentation were analysed; the 'fewer than acoustic' comparison is GLMM pair-wise beta = -0.859, SE = 0.323, z = -2.66, P = 0.007, and the acoustic versus multimodal comparison (cut from the quote) beta = 0.583, SE = 0.302, z = 1.93, P = 0.054, a trend; across all stimuli the 31 males gave 21 calls, 19 taps and 83 foot flags (68% foot flags); the visual-only stimulus was a model foot flag with no live male, so a comparison to a no-stimulus control for the visual condition was not read; no foot-flagging by Micrixalus saxicola, the second species, which is not filed here
